$comment: Authored guides for the Interview + Projects track (s27-s29). Answer structures, percentile maths, trade-off selection and pattern decision maps are all executable Python, so scripts/guides.cjs captures real stdout. These guides tie the authored question bank back to how the answer is actually delivered.

guides.title: Interview Answer Structures & Trade-offs
guides.what: Structured answer = fixed skeleton + ek measurable result. Technical me problem → approach → trade-off → result, behavioural me STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result), aur dono me 60-90 second ka time budget.
guides.why: Interviewer ke paas 45 minute hote hain aur wo signal dhoondhte hain: kya tum trade-offs sochte ho, kya numbers ke saath baat karte ho, aur kya honest ho. Structure ke bina achha kaam bhi adhoora lagta hai.
guides.whereUsed: Technical rounds, behavioural rounds, project deep-dives, aur salary/negotiation conversations.
prereqs: Ek real project (ya course project) jiska data tumhare paas ho
guides.howItWorks: Skeleton ka kaam hai attention ko content par laana. Har jawab me teen layer rakho: context (problem + constraint), decision (option + kyun), proof (number/outcome). Aur last me ek 'kya alag karta' line — ye senior signal hai kyunki isse pata chalta hai ki tumne result ke baad socha.

explain: STAR ke chaar slots fix hote hain, isliye jawab me koi part bhoolna mushkil ho jata hai.
Result me number hona chahiye (0.62 → 0.86) — 'bahut improve hua' koi evidence nahi hai.
Action me lever ka naam hai (table-aware chunking, hybrid retrieval) — interviewer isi par follow-up karega.

examples.code:
lat = [120, 130, 125, 140, 360, 400]
lat.sort()

def pct(xs, p):
    if not xs:
        return None
    k = (len(xs) - 1) * p
    lo, hi = int(k), min(int(k) + 1, len(xs) - 1)
    return xs[lo] + (xs[hi] - xs[lo]) * (k - lo)

import statistics
print("p50", pct(lat, 0.5), "p95", pct(lat, 0.95), "max", max(lat))
print("mean", round(statistics.mean(lat), 1))
print("tail ratio", round(pct(lat, 0.95) / pct(lat, 0.5), 2))
explain: Percentile interpolation se p50/p95 nikalte hain — average ke bajaye tail experience describe karna strong hota hai.
Mean (212.5) aur p95 (390.0) ka bada farq batata hai ki kuch requests outliers hain (cold start/dependency).
Tail ratio (p95/p50) ek line me 'kitna bura worst case hai' bata deta hai — interviewer ise instantly samajhta hai.

examples.code:
options = [
    {"name": "greedy", "cost": "low", "quality": 0.62, "latency_ms": 120},
    {"name": "hybrid+rerank", "cost": "mid", "quality": 0.86, "latency_ms": 400},
    {"name": "hybrid+rerank+cache", "cost": "mid", "quality": 0.86, "latency_ms": 180},
]

def pick(options, quality_bar, latency_budget):
    ok = [o for o in options
          if o["quality"] >= quality_bar and o["latency_ms"] <= latency_budget]
    return min(ok, key=lambda o: (o["latency_ms"], o["cost"]))["name"] if ok else None

print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.8, latency_budget=500))
print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.9, latency_budget=500))
print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.6, latency_budget=200))
explain: Trade-off ko explicit constraint (quality bar + latency budget) me likha gaya — isi tarah interview me bolo: 'budget ye tha, isliye ye chuna'.
Jab koi option bar meet nahi karta to None lauta rahe hain — yahi honest jawab hai: 'is budget me koi option nahi tha, isliye main constraint change karne ko bolta'.
Sorting key (latency, phir cost) decision ko deterministic banati hai — 'kyun ye option' ka jawab reproducible ho jata hai.

howToCode.detail: Har jawab: context → decision → proof → next step. Behavioural ke liye STAR, technical ke liye problem-tradeoff-result.
howToCode.code:
context: problem + constraint
decision: option + reason
proof: number
next: kya alag karta

howToCode.detail: 3-4 numbers yaad karo (scale, latency, accuracy/cost) aur har number ka source bata sako — 'kitne cases par measure kiya'.
Timer ke saath bolkar practice karo; lamba jawab interviewer ke follow-up ke liye jagah nahi chhodta.

howToCode.step: Ek honest 'kya alag karta' line rakho
howToCode.detail: Result ke baad ek improvement/lesson bolo — ye senior signal hai, aur follow-up ko tumhari direction me le jaata hai.

commonMistakes: Numbers ke bina claim ('bahut improve hua', 'large scale', 'fast').
30+ minute ka 'tell me about yourself' (focus kho jata hai).
Sirf tools list karna, decisions na batana.
Failure ka jawab defensive tone me dena (blame) — seniority opposite dikhti hai.
Follow-up par atak jana kyunki metrics/metric source yaad nahi.
bestPractices: Har claim ke saath ek number aur us number ka source.
Answer me ek explicit trade-off mention karo (choice + reason + cost).
Behavioural me 'I' se bolo (team ne kya nahi, maine kya kiya).
Feedback ka jawab curiosity se do: 'koi specific example de sakte ho?'
Ant me 2-3 thoughtful questions poochho (team challenge, success definition, next steps).
guides.realWorld: Interview me project deep-dive ke waqt yahi skeleton chalta hai, aur perform review me bhi — context → decision → metric hota hai. Production me incident postmortem likhna bhi isi structure par hota hai (symptom → measurement → fix → verification).

practice.text: Apne ek project ka 60-second answer likho (context, decision, number, lesson) — aur word count count karo.
Apne project ke latency numbers se p50/p95/max nikalo aur tail ratio explain karo.
Ek trade-off table banao (3 options, quality/latency/cost) aur batao kis budget me kaunsa chunte aur kyun.

interview.q: 'Tell me about yourself' ka best structure?
interview.a: Teen part: ab kya karte ho, ek relevant proof point number ke saath, aur is specific role me kyun — 90 second max.

interview.q: Average ke bajaye p95 kyun bolo?
interview.a: Average tail chhupa deta hai; p95 batata hai ki 1 in 20 request kitni slow hai — interviewer us experience ko judge karta hai.

interview.q: Failure ka sawal kaise handle karoge?
interview.a: Failure + impact + diagnosis + fix + permanent change (test/process). Blame-free aur measurable — yahi strength dikhata hai.

guides.miniChallenge: Apne project ke liye ek 'metrics card' banao: scale, latency p50/p95, quality metric, cost per task — har number ka source likho.
guides.debugTask: Ek follow-up par tum atak gaye (chunk size kyun 800 tha?). Root cause batao aur aage ke liye kya prepare karoge?
revision: Har claim ke saath number + source
guides.interviewTip: Agar interviewer 'ek number do' bole to turant ek do aur uska source batao — number ke bina confidence claim ka koi weight nahi hota.

guides.title: Coding Patterns Decision Map
guides.what: Coding round me pattern recall kaam aata hai: problem ke signals se data structure aur technique chunna (hash-map, two-pointer, sliding window, binary search, heap, DP, graph traversal).
guides.why: Har problem naye sire se solve karne me time khatam ho jata hai. Signals → pattern map hone se approach 30 second me nikal jati hai aur baaki time complexity aur edge cases par lagta hai.
guides.whereUsed: DSA rounds, online assessments, aur production me bhi (streaming metrics, dedupe, batching, top-K).
guides.howItWorks: Constraints hi hint dete hain: n = 1e5 → O(n log n) ya O(n) chahiye, n = 20 → exponential/bitmask, memory tight → streaming. Uske baad do sawal: kya lookup/grouping hai (hash), kya monotonic/sorted hai (two-pointer/binary search), kya repeated subproblem hai (DP).
guides.syntax:
# decision map (signals -> pattern)
lookup/complement/grouping      -> hash map / set      O(n) time
sorted + pair/window           -> two-pointer          O(n) time, O(1) space
contiguous subarray + condition -> sliding window      O(n) time
sorted + value predicate       -> binary search        O(log n)
top-K / streaming max-min      -> heap                 O(n log k)
overlapping subproblems        -> DP                   states x transitions
reachability/levels/ordering   -> BFS/DFS (queue/stack) O(V+E)

explain: Hash map se O(n^2) brute force O(n) ban jata hai: complement dhoondhna ek O(1) lookup hai.
Pehle check karte hain ki complement mila kya, phir current value store karte hain — isse same element do baar use nahi hota.
Khaali input aur no-solution case defined output dete hain (None) — edge cases bolkar test karna strong signal hai.

examples.code:
def longest_unique(s):
    seen, start, best = {}, 0, 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch in seen and seen[ch] >= start:
            start = seen[ch] + 1
        seen[ch] = i
        best = max(best, i - start + 1)
    return best

print(longest_unique("abcabcbb"))
print(longest_unique(""))
print(longest_unique("bbbbb"))
print(longest_unique("abba"))
explain: Sliding window: window ka start sirf aage badhta hai, isliye total work O(n) rehta hai (har character ek baar add, ek baar remove).
seen[ch] >= start check zaroori hai — warna purana index window ke bahar wale character par start peeche chala jata.
Edge cases (khaali string, repeated characters, 'abba' jaisa trap) explicitly print kiye gaye.

examples.code:
PATTERNS = [
    {"name": "hash-map", "when": "lookup complement grouping",
     "cost": "O(n) time, O(n) space"},
    {"name": "two-pointer", "when": "sorted monotonic window",
     "cost": "O(n) time, O(1) space"},
    {"name": "binary-search", "when": "sorted predicate on value", "cost": "O(log n)"},
    {"name": "heap", "when": "top-K streaming max-min", "cost": "O(n log k)"},
    {"name": "DP", "when": "overlapping subproblems optimal substructure",
     "cost": "states x transitions"},
]

def suggest(signals):
    return [p["name"] for p in PATTERNS if any(s in p["when"] for s in signals)]

print(suggest(["sorted", "monotonic"]))
print(suggest(["top-K", "streaming"]))
print(suggest(["overlapping"]))
print(suggest(["lookup"]))
explain: Pattern selection ko data banaya gaya hai — interview me tum 'signals se pattern' wali table bolkar approach justify kar sakte ho.
Ek signal multiple pattern suggest kar sakta hai ('sorted' → two-pointer ya binary search) — us waqt constraint (space/time) se decide karo.
Har pattern ke saath complexity likhi hai, isliye jawab me time aur space dono claim ho jate hain.

howToCode.detail: n ka size likho aur usse allowed complexity nikalo — n = 1e5 par O(n^2) nahi chalega, n = 20 par exponential ya bitmask theek hai.
Sorted? Monotonic? Contiguous? Lookup/grouping? Repeated subproblem? Ek signal mil gaya to approach 30 second me clear ho jati hai.
howToCode.code:
if is_sorted(nums): two_pointer()
elif need_lookup: hash_map()

howToCode.detail: Brute force + uski complexity bolo, bottleneck identify karo, phir data structure/patteren badlo — interviewer ko process dikhta hai.

howToCode.step: Edge cases likh kar test karo
howToCode.detail: Empty, single element, duplicates, negative, all-same, max size — solution likhne ke baad khud hi bolo aur trace karo.

commonMistakes: Constraints padhe bina solution likhna (n = 1e5 par O(n^2) propose karna).
Two-pointer bina monotonic property ke lagana (silent galat answer).
Hash map ka worst case (O(n) collisions) ya extra space mention na karna.
Silent coding — approach verbalize na karna.
bestPractices: Har jawab me complexity (time + space) explicitly bolo.
Approach pehle verbalize karo, phir code likho.
Test cases teen bucket me socho: small, typical, edge.
Library functions allowed hone par bolo: 'production me Counter use karunga, algorithm core yahan likh raha hoon'.
Interviewer ke bug par argument nahi — acknowledge, trace, fix, aur wahi test add karo.
guides.realWorld: Ye patterns production me bhi aate hain: dedupe/grouping (hash), rate limiting (sliding window), top-K frequent queries (heap), retry scheduling (binary search on time), aur dependency ordering (graph traversal). Coding round ki tayari asal me system design ki tayari bhi hai.

practice.text: two_sum hash map se solve karo aur uski complexity dono case (average, worst) me batao.
Sliding window se minimum length subarray nikalo jiska sum target se bada ho.
Ek 'signals → pattern' table banao apne 10 practice problems ke liye aur likho kis signal ne kaunsa pattern diya.

interview.q: O(n^2) ko optimize karne ka pehla step?
interview.a: Bottleneck identify karo: dobara kya compute ho raha hai? Lookup hai to hash/set, sorted property hai to two-pointer/binary search, repeated subproblem hai to DP.
Jab monotonic property ho — sorted array, ya window me add/remove se condition predictably badle. Bina monotonicity ke pointer movement ka logic galat ho jata hai.

interview.q: Hash map ka worst case kab O(n) ho jata hai?
interview.a: Collisions zyada hone par (bura hash ya adversarial keys) lookup O(n) ho jata hai — isliye average aur worst case dono bolna sahi hai.

guides.miniChallenge: Top-K frequent elements nikalo (streaming input, bounded memory) — hash + heap ka combo use karo aur complexity likho.
guides.debugTask: Sliding window solution interview me ek test case par fail hua (window ke bahar ka purana index use kiya gaya). Bug reproduce karo aur fix likho.
revision: Signals: sorted, monotonic, contiguous, lookup, subproblem
Hash O(n), two-pointer O(1) space, heap O(n log k)
guides.interviewTip: Interviewer ki help se approach nikalo: 'kya main maan sakta hoon ki input sorted hai?' jaisa sawal galat direction se bacha leta hai aur collaboration dikhata hai.

guides.title: Resume Project Defense Playbook
guides.what: Project defense = 60-second pitch + evidence card + honest boundaries. Interviewer tumhare system ke numbers, failures aur decisions sunna chahta hai — tool list nahi.
guides.why: Resume par project likhna aasan hai; uski depth prove karna mushkil. Jo candidates numbers, trade-offs aur 'kya alag karta' bata paate hain, unka project 'tutorial' nahi lagta.
guides.whereUsed: Portfolio projects, final-year projects, capstone, aur internal projects (promotion/promo conversations me bhi).
guides.howItWorks: Defense teen cheezon par khada hai: (1) architecture ek line me (client → API → data flow), (2) evidence — measured numbers aur unka source, (3) failure stories — kya toota, kaise detect hua, kaise fix hua. Sabse strong signal: '3 numbers jo mera kaam prove karte hain' aur ek honest 'dobara banata to kya alag karta'.
guides.syntax:
# 60-second pitch
problem+scale (10s) -> my role (10s) -> approach + tradeoff (15s)
-> measured result (10s) -> lesson + next step (15s)

# evidence card
evidence = {"recall@5": (0.62, 0.86), "p95_ms": (1400, 400)}

examples.code:
sections = [
    ("problem + scale", 10),
    ("my role + constraints", 10),
    ("approach + tradeoff", 15),
    ("measured result", 10),
    ("lesson + next step", 15),
]

total = sum(s for _, s in sections)
print(total, "seconds")
for name, secs in sections:
    print(f"{name:<22} {secs:>3}s")
print("fits 60s:", total <= 60)
explain: Pitch ko time budget me toda gaya — isse jawab khatam hone se pehle interview ko dikh jata hai ki structure hai.
Har section ka second count likhne se practice me pata chalta hai kahan time zyada jaa raha hai.
Ant me lesson + next step rakhna deliberate hai: ye hissa sabse strong senior signal hai.
Evidence card me har metric ka before → after aur % change hai — interviewer numbers ko instantly verify kar sakta hai.
Lower-is-better metrics (latency, cost) ka negative % improvement dikhata hai; direction ko naam ke saath samjhao (p95 1400 → 400ms).
Ye bhi print kiya gaya ki numbers kis dataset par measure hue — bina source ke number ka weight kam ho jata hai.
Defense me har expected question ke do hisse hote hain: ek number (current state) aur ek plan (next step). Ek missing ho to jawab aadha lagta hai.
Gaps ko print karke rehearsal list ban jati hai — practice targeted ho jaati hai, generic nahi.
Ye pattern interview se pehle ek baar chalane se 'kya poocha ja sakta hai' ka checklist ban jata hai.

howToCode.detail: Client → API → services → data stores; arrows par protocol/async. Framework names baad me, data flow pehle.
4 numbers likho: scale, latency (p50/p95), quality metric, cost — har ek ka source (dataset size, tool, date).
Ek incident: symptom → measurement → fix → verification. Yahi story 'kya tum production sochte ho' ka jawab hai.
Kya solve nahi karta (freshness lag, high-stakes decisions) — scope honest bolna maturity dikhata hai.

commonMistakes: Frameworks ki list dena bina data flow ya trade-off batane ke.
Numbers yaad na hona (kitne rows, kaun sa chunk size, kaun sa index).
Demo reproduce na ho paana (data/branch/environment alag).
Sirf happy path batana — failure aur degraded mode ka koi zikr nahi.
Team project me apna contribution unclear chhodna.
bestPractices: Seeded sample data + README steps rakho taaki demo reproducible ho.
Har number ka source likho (kis dataset par, kab measure kiya).
Decision log (ADR) maintain karo — 'kya alag karta' ka material wahi se aata hai.
Degraded modes likho (dependency down par kya hota hai) aur ek test se prove karo.
Claim ko bound karo: 'is data par ye metric' — global claim se bacho.
guides.realWorld: Portfolio project ka interview round, capstone viva, aur internal design review — teeno me yahi playbook chalti hai. Interview me 'teen numbers do jo mera kaam prove karte hain' ka ready jawab alag level par rakhta hai.

practice.text: Apne project ka 60-second pitch likho aur time budget ke saath mark karo.
Apna evidence card banao (4 metrics, before → after, source) aur deltas calculate karo.
10 expected defense questions ki list banao aur har ek ke liye number + plan likho.

interview.q: System kitna scale karega — kaise answer karoge?
interview.a: Current measured state + bottleneck + plan: '20 rps par p95 400ms, bottleneck DB connections aur vector index; plan read replicas + caching + sharding'.
Eval set size, per-bucket breakdown aur limitation batao: chhote buckets par 'insufficient data' — overclaiming se better hai honest confidence interval.

interview.q: Dependency failure par system kya karta hai?
interview.a: Degraded modes named hon: retrieval down → retry with message, model down → fallback provider, DB slow → cached response. Aur har mode test se proven.

guides.miniChallenge: Apne project ka ek 'defense card' banao: architecture ek line, 4 numbers source ke saath, 2 failure stories, aur 2 known boundaries.
guides.debugTask: Interviewer ne tumhari claim ('p95 400ms') par poocha 'kis load par?' — ye kya batata hai, aur aage ke liye kya prepare karoge?
revision: Pitch: problem → role → tradeoff → number → lesson
Evidence card me har number ka source
guides.interviewTip: Interview ke ant me khud ek limitation batao ('freshness async refresh se hai, realtime nahi') — honest boundary batana overclaiming se zyada credibility deta hai.
